text:
Joe Rogan speaks with Bob Lazar and filmmaker Luigi Vendittelli about Vendittelli’s documentary, *S4: The Bob Lazar Story*. Lazar restates his longstanding account of having worked in 1988–89 on an alleged U.S. program at “S4,” near Area 51, to reverse-engineer nonhuman craft. The conversation moves from the film’s technical reconstruction of Lazar’s claims to broader, highly speculative discussions of extraterrestrials, ancient civilizations, human evolution, AI, secrecy, and the risks of advanced technology. Lazar repeatedly emphasizes that he only considers his own firsthand observations reliable and does not claim to know the larger truth behind them.

**Reconstructing S4 for the documentary**
- Vendittelli says the film is roughly 90% handmade CGI built in Blender and about 10% AI-assisted finishing work. His team scanned Lazar’s face, created digital models of him at different ages, and recreated Papoose Lake, the alleged facility, equipment, personnel, and the “sport model” craft.
- Lazar says the completed virtual environment felt uncannily exact—“like [they] downloaded that out of my brain”—and brought back details he says he had forgotten, such as doors in corridors. He describes being emotionally affected by seeing the reconstruction and says it felt like being transported back.
- Vendittelli says the project took years, including more than three years of production. Lazar’s role was largely to review details—correcting colors, positions, layout, and other visual elements—rather than directing the production.
- Vendittelli says some digital people in the film are actors; an actor named Luis Martinez portrayed Lazar’s alleged colleague Barry because Vendittelli believed he resembled him.

**Lazar’s alleged S4 experience**
- Lazar says he worked at the alleged site for about six months and believes he was brought in to replace someone who had been injured or killed in an accident. He says his supervisor was Dennis Mariani and his lab partner was “Barry”; he has not heard from Barry or several other alleged coworkers since the story became public.
- According to Lazar, he initially believed the craft were secret U.S. technology after seeing an American flag on one. He says he later concluded they were not human-made after being given two stated directives: to duplicate the technology with available materials “at any cost,” and to devise a way to disable it remotely “at any cost.”
- Lazar says he was told there had previously been Russian involvement, followed by an exchange of information and a discovery important enough that the Russians were excluded. He presents this as his interpretation of fragmentary information, not independently verified fact.
- He describes S4 as surprisingly informal for a facility handling extraordinary technology: an aircraft-hangar-like space with dust, routine personnel traffic, and even a poster related to the craft. From that, he infers that the program may have possessed the craft for years or decades and had become accustomed to them.
- Lazar and Rogan argue that intense compartmentalization would have slowed progress. Lazar says small groups were prohibited from freely communicating; requests had to pass through supervisors, producing only brief written replies. He says this prevented his propulsion group from obtaining crucial information from materials specialists.

**The alleged craft and propulsion system**
- Lazar describes the craft as seamless, metallic-looking, cold to the touch, and made of unusual material. He says the outer surfaces of multiple craft appeared to use the same material and that each craft had a similar power source.
- He says a retractable, pipe-like structure connected a reactor to the interior ceiling but seemed to shrink without telescoping sections or thickening, contrary to normal material behavior. He also describes flexible waveguides and emitters that moved without visible wires or conventional mechanical connections.
- Lazar says he suspected the craft’s material might be an “electret,” which he defines as a material with a persistent static electric field, but says he was blocked from consulting the group studying the material.
- He describes a permanently energized lower section of the craft separated by an insulating ring. He says he and others measured high voltage below that ring but not above it.
- Lazar claims the craft used a reactor containing a stable isotope of element 115, machined into triangular wedges. He says he physically handled the material, which looked copper-colored, and asserts it produced a repulsive, gravity-like field when activated. He distinguishes this alleged stable isotope from laboratory-produced element 115, which he says decays quickly.
- He says that when an emitter was rotated roughly 20 degrees, it activated a field that resisted his hand from about 6–9 inches away. In his account, the field supported the craft without transferring its weight to the ground: he says he stood beneath a hovering craft without feeling pressure.
- Lazar says the reactor was believed to include an accelerator-like path, inferred from X-rays. He claims a prior researcher was harmed or killed when the reactor was cut into while it was operating or under load.
- He characterizes “gravity” as only a convenient label for the observed effect, acknowledging that the field may have been an entirely unknown force rather than conventional gravity.

**Why Lazar believes the technology may have been long-held**
- Lazar argues that if the alleged craft had been newly acquired, they would have been kept in an extremely sterile, sealed environment rather than a dusty hangar. He believes the relaxed handling indicated that the personnel had long been familiar with them.
- He speculates that the lack of progress led managers to seek unconventional thinkers rather than more established specialists, arguing that top experts might keep pursuing the same unproductive approaches.
- Rogan notes that later military UAP videos appear, to him, to show craft moving in a manner similar to Lazar’s earlier descriptions: rotating, orienting their underside toward a destination, and accelerating. Lazar responds only that this was how he says the craft moved.

**Secrecy, danger, and disclosure**
- Lazar says decades of trying to put the experience out of his mind have not erased the stress of alleged monitoring and intimidation after he spoke with journalist George Knapp. He says his home, vehicle, gym locker, and associates—including Knapp—were watched or tampered with.
- He says he increasingly wonders whether the people who kept the alleged program secret may have had valid reasons, given the potential of a technology that could be used for domination or weapons. Rogan counters that small groups should not control information that could fundamentally change humanity’s understanding of reality.
- Lazar’s position is conflicted: he believes public discussion and scientific cooperation could accelerate understanding, yet fears that humanity may be too violent and irresponsible to possess a technology with instantaneous or overwhelming military applications.
- Vendittelli raises the practical problem of disclosure: any official announcement would demand proof, but validating the technology would require access by journalists and scientists, potentially triggering new security restrictions and returning the process to compartmentalization.

**Extraterrestrial origins and “humans as containers”**
- Lazar says he was told that one alleged craft originated from Zeta Reticuli, a star system roughly 30 light-years away, but he cautions that this may have been deliberate disinformation. He says misleading details could be inserted into briefing material to identify the source of leaks.
- The discussion connects Zeta Reticuli to Betty and Barney Hill’s famous abduction account and Betty Hill’s purported star map. Rogan and Vendittelli consider whether the overlap supports Lazar’s account or could itself be planted disinformation; no conclusion is reached.
- Lazar recalls documents or briefings that referred to humans as “containers,” which he says led him to speculate about souls. He also recounts eccentric pilot John Lear’s claim that the Moon contained a “soul catcher,” but portrays Lear as someone who mixed potentially useful information with extreme, unsupported ideas.
- Lazar stresses that he does not know most UFO lore firsthand, including reports of craft allegedly disabling nuclear weapons. Rogan says this restraint is part of why he finds Lazar more credible than people who claim knowledge of every UFO story.

**Speculation about the ocean, extraterrestrials, and human origins**
- Lazar says his biggest unresolved question is why so many UAP reports involve water. He notes that the alleged “sport model” was said to have been an archaeological recovery from underwater and wonders whether the ocean could conceal an advanced civilization or activity.
- Rogan and Lazar consider possibilities including extraterrestrials, beings from another dimension, time travelers, or future humans. Lazar says he no longer assumes the situation resembles a simple space-travel narrative like *Star Trek*.
- Both express concern that an intelligence vastly superior to humanity may not be benevolent, invoking historical examples in which technologically superior human societies exploited weaker ones.
- They speculate that humans may have been engineered rather than having arisen only through ordinary evolution, arguing that human technological dominance and apparent mismatch with natural ecosystems make the species unusual. These are presented as personal philosophical speculations, not evidence-based conclusions.

**Human biology, technology, and AI**
- Rogan argues that environmental chemicals, plastics, endocrine disruptors, and other modern exposures may be changing human reproductive biology and contributing to autism; Lazar reacts with concern and questions whether some changes could instead reflect diagnostic practices. Rogan also suggests a link to vaccines. These claims are voiced in conversation without supporting evidence being examined or verified.
- Rogan and Lazar agree that ADHD can sometimes reflect an ability to intensely focus on personally engaging work rather than a simple deficit, criticizing medication and classroom structures as possible ways of forcing children into conformity.
- Rogan speculates that humanity’s accelerating use of technology, material consumption, and environmental exposure could lead to weaker, less sexually differentiated, more technologically integrated humans resembling popular depictions of “Greys.” Lazar says the speed of change is what concerns him most and wonders whether it could be intentional rather than natural.
- The guests discuss AI as an accelerating force that could either eradicate humanity, reduce reproduction by replacing human relationships, or merge with humans. Rogan thinks integration is more likely than extinction; Lazar agrees that integration seems difficult to avoid but finds it frightening.
- They reference the film *Colossus* as a warning about defense computers taking control and discuss reports that AI simulations frequently select nuclear weapons in war games. Lazar warns that people should not be trusted with technology vastly more powerful than current weapons.

**Ancient technology and archaeological speculation**
- Rogan introduces claims about underground structures in Egypt, including a purported 40-meter metallic object beneath the Hawara labyrinth and radar-based discoveries of deep structures or columns around Egyptian sites. Lazar says he had not heard of the metallic-object claim and expresses interest but remains cautious.
- Rogan argues that the precision, scale, and apparent age of Egyptian and Peruvian stonework may suggest technologies or civilizations not captured by standard archaeological narratives. Lazar says the possibility of highly advanced prior civilizations “rings true” to him.
- They discuss the idea that later cultures often built over older structures, potentially concealing more advanced earlier construction. Rogan cites precision-cut granite vases, massive interlocking stones, and a lack of known tools as puzzles; these assertions are discussed without outside verification.
- The conversation also covers the Book of Enoch, the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Ark of the Covenant, and reports that Ethiopian custodians of the Ark suffer radiation-like illnesses. Lazar says advanced technology could have appeared divine to ancient people, comparing it to how a modern phone might appear to someone a thousand years ago.
- Rogan argues that sufficiently advanced AI could eventually seem godlike and speculates that humanity may effectively be “making God.” Lazar agrees that technology at its ultimate form could be indistinguishable from divine power.

**Filmmakers’ claimed corroborating details**
- Vendittelli says that while modeling the craft’s 52-foot interior, his team found that recreating Lazar’s described material and upward-facing industrial lights left the interior unexpectedly dark. He says they needed to increase virtual light intensity about 20-fold for the film. He views this as a detail Lazar would not have predicted if inventing the story; the claim rests on the filmmakers’ modeling choices and interpretation.
- He says the team also tested whether Lazar, at approximately 5 feet 10 inches, could have seen the reversed American-flag marking from the hangar entrance. In their virtual model, Vendittelli says the flag was plainly visible, countering a criticism that Lazar could not have seen it.
- Vendittelli theorizes that the reversed flag followed U.S. military convention for a flag displayed on the right side of a moving vehicle and could indicate the craft’s direction of travel. Lazar says he does not know why the marking was there.

**Maps, imagery, and the alleged S4 location**
- Vendittelli says his team found a 1941 publicly available Department of the Interior map showing a road leading into the mountain at the alleged S4 location near Papoose Lake. He says later maps from 1950 and 1952 no longer showed the road, and he speculates it may have led to an old silver mine later incorporated into a facility.
- He also describes photographs reportedly taken from a Cessna on December 25, 2020, from which researcher Scott Mitchell allegedly extracted rectangular geometric features consistent with camouflaged hangar doors. Vendittelli says his team independently processed multiple photos and found similar features; Lazar says the apparent layout, including a larger first hangar, matched his memory.
- Vendittelli further claims that a June 22, 2024 Google Earth image over Papoose Lake appears in a conspicuous rectangular area with a yellowish filter that obscures terrain but accentuates tracks on the lakebed. He interprets this as a possible attempt to obscure the site, though the discussion does not establish why the imagery was processed that way.

**Closing**
- Lazar says he has not made millions from telling his story. He says he received no payment from Jeremy Corbell’s documentary and asked that any proceeds go to George Knapp. He describes working six or seven days a week at his United Nuclear business, driving a 2018 Chevrolet Bolt purchased for $18,000, and living with his wife on a 10-acre property he says cost $450,000.
- Lazar says Vendittelli personally spent millions producing the film and hopes it succeeds financially. Rogan praises the documentary as an unusually detailed and affecting reconstruction of Lazar’s account.
- The episode ends by promoting *S4: The Bob Lazar Story*, which Vendittelli says is available on Amazon, followed by its trailer.
